case.pattern_description: Several cards belonging to different customers transacted through one rare device profile inside a short window: 19 cards across 20 customers on 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080', a profile seen on only 52 cards bank-wide. This is coordinated use of a single machine across unrelated accounts rather than the compromise of one cardholder, so it fits none of the five documented patterns. It was found by expanding from the flagged transaction to its device profile and back out to every other card that touched it.

Policy rule R9: Undocumented patterns: R9. Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Policy rule R6: Shared origin: R6. Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.
Cardholder denies the transaction on contact

Policy rule R2: Customer denies the transaction: R2. Customer denies the transaction. Recommend `BLOCK_CARD` and `CREATE_CASE`. Add `FILE_REPORT` if exposure exceeds $1,000 or the case connects to a shared device profile or another card's fraud.

case.summary: The analyst opened this review on case ID C13487-K1 after observing several cards transacting through the same unusual device profile, and the cardholder denied the $74.96 online transaction on 2016-11-22 on card C13487-K1. The connection came through an anonymising proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS) from named hardware (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M) marked New, a combination that appeared in 190 of 590,742 transactions and on 4 of 9 confirmed fraud cases with no documented pattern. The device profile was shared with 19 other cards across 20 customers within the 30-day window and named per policy R6, while 83% of cleared alarms and 18% of confirmed fraud used a New device, and the card's 5% online history was mildly exculpatory at 11.9% of cleared versus 4.5% of confirmed fraud. The transaction was assessed as undocumented fraud at probability 0.90, matching 5 closed cases (CC-3035, CC-2971, CC-0017, CC-4259, CC-3520) that closed as 2 confirmed fraud and 3 cleared, with exposure of $74.96. The external email-domain 'yahoo.com' was classified as a free webmail address appearing on 3,667 confirmed frauds and 573 cleared alarms with no weight, and policy R2 recommended BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE because the customer denied the transaction.

sar.narrative: Between 2016-11-22 and 2016-11-22, card C13487-K1 belonging to customer C13487 was used for 1 transaction(s) totalling $74.96, of which the transaction that triggered this investigation was $74.96 on 2016-11-22. The activity was conducted online under product code C, billed in region 191.0, from the device profile 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080'. The connection came through an anonymising proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS) from a device marked New for the account on named hardware (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M). Cardholder denies the transaction on contact. A fraud analyst opened this review after seeing several cards transacting through the same unusual device profile. The same device profile was used by 19 other card(s) in the thirty days to 2016-11-22 (C01289-K1, C01996-K2, C02910-K1, C02975-K1, C03676-K2, C04108-K2), indicating a common actor operating across more than one cardholder. On contact, cardholder states they did not make the transaction and still holds the card. That response is an assumption recorded in the case file, as no cardholder replies were available to this investigation. The activity is suspicious because it fits none of the five fraud patterns the institution documents, while showing the coordination described above. It is assessed at a 90% probability of being fraudulent on 5 independent pieces of evidence drawn from the transaction graph and the institution's closed-case history. The filing is made because the activity is coordinated across accounts and matches no documented pattern, which requires a report regardless of amount. The total amount of suspicious activity is $74.96. The card has been blocked and scheduled for reissue, an internal investigation case has been opened, the cards sharing the same origin have been placed under monitoring, and the matter has been escalated to a fraud analyst.
